subject: Clarification: data-hold scope for ArtiHealth (tenant log preservation & evidence)
messages:
From: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@artihealth.com>

Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@artihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarification on log preservation and SIG answers for EU patient tenants

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the call today. We attached an updated SIG/CAIQ matrix (see artihealth_SIG_questions_v2.xlsx) with two focused asks under "Data retention / Logging":

1) For tenant-scoped session logs that include request metadata (IP, timestamp, non-PHI prompts), our legal team needs confirmation whether Redwood can commit to a customer-requested preservation hold window of 24 months (for forensics) for EU-based tenants.
2) If Redwood cannot natively retain tenant session logs for 24 months on hosted plans, what are the supported mechanisms to export, escrow, or store that data for the requested window while remaining within Redwood's compliance boundary?

We need short, technical answers suitable for our security review and for inclusion with our SIG uplift. Can you also include any SOC 2 attestation references or a pointer to the log-retention page?

Appreciate a pragmatic proposal (ops steps + ownership + timeline).

—Lena
Security Compliance, ArtiHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@artihealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification on log preservation and SIG answers for EU patient tenants

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear asks and the updated XLSX. I pulled in Marissa (Customer Success) to scope operational ownership and we'll brief Security for the technical details. High level answers below; Rishi will follow with the precise runtime/evidence steps.

Short answers up front:
- Can Redwood commit to a 24-month tenant preservation window for hosted customers? Not by default on the standard hosted tier. Default session/log TTL for hosted ephemeral request logs is 30 days.
- Mechanisms for customers to preserve 24 months of tenant logs: 1) Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment with customer-configured long-term persistence, or 2) automated periodic exports (S3) to a customer-controlled bucket + verified export checksum + export retention policy (Redwood managed export job).

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP):
1) We’ll provide a technical statement and SOC 2 reference (48 hours).
2) Rishi will produce a step-by-step export and verification playbook for storing tenant logs in an EU-region S3 or your SIEM, plus any PII redaction options.
3) Marissa will propose an operational SLA and cost estimate for the export + storage workflow (since prolonged retention beyond default has a unit cost).
4) If you need Redwood to host retained logs for the 24-month window, we can discuss Dedicated capacity or Private deployment pricing and timeline.

I’ve attached our public log policy (redwood_log-retention-policy_v1.pdf) and flagged the key bits for you.

Karthik
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@artihealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification on log preservation and SIG answers for EU patient tenants

Hi Lena — adding the technical detail you can paste into the SIG/CAIQ. I kept the answers concise and included a short evidence checklist at the end.

1) Default behavior and TTL
- Hosted (default): session/request metadata and ephemeral inference logs are retained for 30 days by default for debugging and monitoring. The raw model input/output (for customers who opt in to logging) is treated as customer content and follows tenant privacy settings; by default model content mirrors the 30-day session TTL unless you select longer retention at tenant level (not available on self-serve hosted currently).

2) Options to meet a 24-month preservation requirement
A) Export approach (recommended, fastest to implement):
   - Configure an automated export job (weekly full + daily incremental) that ships tenant-scoped session logs to an ArtiHealth-managed EU S3 bucket (we support AWS EU regions). Exports are delivered encrypted (AES-256) in transit and at rest; we support delivery with client-side KMS if you require your own CMK.
   - Export job generates a manifest + SHA256 checksum for each archive. Redwood stores the last 90 days of export job logs for verification.
   - You (customer) own the exported retention policy (24 months) and audit controls.

B) Dedicated/Private:
   - On Dedicated or Private, tenant storage TTL is configurable. We can configure a 24-month retention window in your dedicated pool and apply stricter access controls / KMS keys. This requires contract changes.

3) Data minimization and PII considerations
- If there are PHI elements in conversation text, we can offer an on-export redaction hook (regex-based or rule-based masks) prior to packing archives — this is a custom ops job and needs to be agreed in the MAP.

4) Evidence & attestation we can provide
- SOC 2 Type II report references (control IDs): Logging and Monitoring (CC6), Encryption (CC7) — we will provide our SOC 2 reference page and a signed letter stating which controls cover export integrity and retention practices.
- Export job runbook and sample manifest (CSV + checksums).
- Console snapshots showing tenant retention configuration (for Dedicated) or export job history (for hosted).

Evidence checklist (we will deliver):
- Redacted sample export manifest + two sample archive checksums.
- Step-by-step export playbook (how to set up S3 destination + IAM + KMS).
- SOC 2 pointer and contact for formal attestation.
- If you need a CAIQ update, we’ll annotate the CAIQ answers under (A.1 - Data Protection) with links to the exported playbook.

Operational notes / costs
- Export is billed as export bandwidth + archive storage. Marissa, please add the estimated monthly cost to the MAP.

If that aligns with what you need I’ll package this into a short statement for the SIG (one page) and attach the sample artifacts.

—Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we finalize the SIG answers: 

- Export approach: Can we require server-side KMS + object lock (governance mode) on the destination bucket? We need chain-of-custody proof and object immutability for 24 months.
- Evidence: Please include the manifest + two sample checksums and a console screenshot of an export run (timestamped). For SOC 2, we only need the reference page + the control IDs you mentioned.

If you can deliver the one-page SIG statement and artifacts during next week, we should be able to close this item for our review.

—Lena

Lena — small status update and deliverables. Per Rishi’s plan we finished the artifacts and attached them here:

Deliverables attached to this thread:
- artihealth_SIG_questions_v2.xlsx (your updated worksheet, annotated)
- redwood_log-retention-policy_v1.pdf (public policy)
- sample_export_manifest_20261112.csv (manifest with two sample archive lines + SHA256 checksums)
- export_run_screenshot_20261112.png (console screenshot of the export job run)

Responses to your clarifications:
- Server-side KMS + Object Lock: Supported. We support server-side encryption using customer-managed CMKs and can provide guidance for configuring S3 Object Lock (governance mode). Note: object lock proof is part of the exported artifact chain — we provide manifest + timestamps + archive checksums; object lock configuration is controlled by your S3 bucket policy.
- Chain-of-custody: manifests include UTC timestamps, archive checksums, and the signing metadata (export job id). We will include a short attestation letter referencing the SOC 2 control IDs (Logging/Monitoring CC6, Encryption CC7) and describing the export integrity process.

Next steps: Marissa will send a pricing estimate for scheduled exports vs Dedicated retention. Irene is standing by to draft a short amendment to the contract if you opt for Redwood-hosted retention.

If you'd like a brief walkthrough of the export setup, I can have Marissa schedule a 30-minute run-through next week.

Best,
Karthik
